newsitem.title: JAPAN: DirecTV plans to offer on-demand services in Japan.
newsitem.headline: DirecTV plans to offer on-demand services in Japan.

text.p: Satellite broadcaster DirecTV Japan said on Wednesday that it plans to offer on-demand information services in Japan by mid-1998.
"Many of the interactive contents will be available by the middle of next year," Gareth Chang, chairman of DirecTV Japan, told a news conference.

DirecTV Japan said it would offer interactive multimedia services such as product information from shopping channels and weather and traffic information, using Matsushita Electric Industrial Co Ltd's newly developed still-image carousel broadcasting technology.
The technology will be incorporated into software for set-top boxes for DirecTV's satellite digital broadcasting service, it said.
DirecTV is a partnership between Hughes Electronics Corp's DirecTV International Inc, Matsushita and other Japanese companies.
A Matsushita official told the same news conference that the company plans to seek other broadcasters, both satellite and ground-based, to become partners in the new technology.
A DirecTV Japan official said that the company hopes to sell the set-top boxes for 45,000 yen or less.
Chang said that preparations for starting satellite broadcasting services in Japan were on schedule.
DirecTV Japan is expected to begin broadcasting in November or December this year and to offer 72 to 96 channels. It will be the second operator to begin satellite broadcasting in Japan.
